title: Degreewise finite filtration with acyclic graded complexes is acyclic
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K^\bullet$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, and $F$ a decreasing filtration of $K^\bullet$ by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Write $F^pK^n=\operatorname{im}((F^pK^\bullet\hookrightarrow K^\bullet)^n)$ as in [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Assume that for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ there are integers $\ell_n,h_n$ with $F^{\ell_n}K^n=K^n$ and $F^{h_n}K^n=0$. If every associated graded complex $\operatorname{gr}^p_FK$ is acyclic, meaning its cohomology in every degree is zero, then $K$ is acyclic. No global finite bound on the subcomplex filtration is required.

source.place: Homology, Tag 012W, lemma-biregular-ss-converges, parts (2)--(4), with the zero Serre subcategory

proof.text: Use the associated filtered-complex spectral sequence E and its differential-compatible page-zero isomorphisms. At (p,q), form the short-complex isomorphism from page zero in bidegrees (p,q-1),(p,q),(p,q+1) to the graded complex in degrees p+(q-1),p+q,p+(q+1). The differential equations give the two commutative squares. Acyclicity of the graded complex makes page-zero homology vanish, and E.iso identifies it with page one.

source.place: Homology, Tag 012W, lemma-biregular-ss-converges, parts (2)--(4), with the zero Serre subcategory

proof.text: Induct on the positive page number. A zero page object has zero homology at that bidegree, and the successor-page isomorphism gives a zero object on the next page. Therefore every positive page term is zero.

source.place: Homology, Tag 012W, lemma-biregular-ss-converges, parts (2)--(4), with the zero Serre subcategory

proof.text: Apply degreewiseFiltered_stable_quotient with Y(n)=H^n(K) and identity comparison. It supplies a finite image filtration H(n) and, for each p,n, a tail page t>=1 whose cycle/boundary quotient is its p-th graded piece. The quotient description of E_t at (p,n-p) identifies this quotient with a zero page term. Proof irrelevance identifies the two B<=Z proofs. Hence every graded piece of H(n) is zero.

source.place: Homology, Tag 012W, lemma-biregular-ss-converges, parts (2)--(4), with the zero Serre subcategory

proof.text: A zero graded piece is a zero cokernel of the inclusion of successive filtration steps. This inclusion is epic (Preadditive.epi_of_isZero_cokernel) and monic, hence invertible. Subobject.eq_of_comm makes consecutive steps equal. Induct on a natural-number difference to make any two integer-indexed steps equal. The finite top and bottom bounds give top=bottom, which implies the identity of H^n(K) is zero. Thus H^n(K)=0 for every n.

lean.statement:
theorem degreewiseFiltered_acyclic
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (F : DecreasingFiltration K)
    (hfinite : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ lo hi : ℤ,
      F.complexStep lo n = ⊤ ∧ F.complexStep hi n = ⊥)
    (hgraded : ∀ p : ℤ, (F.gradedPiece p).Acyclic) : K.Acyclic
